diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's CATV service is provisioned and the ONU is online, but CATV synchronization is false. Internet service, EPON optics, VLAN, authentication, router, OLT, and PON-port operation are all normal, indicating an RF/CATV path or ONU CATV-tuner synchronization problem rather than an IP connectivity fault.
evidence: The complaint is TV-only; Internet traffic and authenticated IP sessions are functioning normally.
The subscriber is active, has CATV service enabled, uses a CATV profile and CATV-capable ONU, but catv_synced is 0.
The ONU is online and authenticated, with RX power -20.37 dBm and TX power 2.44 dBm, both within normal EPON thresholds.
Seven days of RX and TX telemetry are stable within the healthy noise limits; distance is constant at 118 and TX bias remains within the healthy range.
All probed ONUs on EPON0/7 respond, ruling out a PON-port or broad splitter failure based on available evidence.
The OLT, router, VLAN 1037, RADIUS records, and session behavior are normal, ruling out OLT, router, provisioning, authentication, and VLAN faults.
No CATV RF measurements are supplied, so the most appropriate closed-list diagnosis is catv_drift with a small residual possibility of a local CATV drop, splitter, or ONU hardware fault.

remediation.action: Check the ONU CATV optical/RF receive level, tuner lock status, and CATV connector/drop/splitter path. Reapply or resynchronize the CATV profile and reboot the CATV-capable ONU. If RF levels are abnormal or synchronization does not return, inspect the customer drop and splitter, then replace the ONU CATV module/ONU if required. Check adjacent CATV subscribers on the same splitter to determine whether the issue is shared.

ground_truth.root_cause: The customer is recorded as subscribed to CATV but catv_synced is 0, so the CATV state was never pushed to the ONU. Data service is unaffected; only the television service is missing.
expected_reasoning: The customer reports working internet and missing television
catv_service is 1 and catv_synced is 0, so the subscription exists and the device state does not match it
The ONU model supports CATV, so this is not an equipment limitation
Optical readings are normal and the live probe confirms the ONU is healthy
Sessions and daily traffic are normal, consistent with working data service
The OLT and router are healthy and no shared fault exists
This is a service state mismatch on one dimension, of the same class as the 84 unsynced lines in the estate
It is resolved by re-pushing the CATV state rather than by any field work
distractors: Every network signal is healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The complaint could be read as customer equipment rather than provisioning
